public_context.environment_introduction:
# Environment Information

## Brief Introduction:  
This environment is a personal health record management system designed for individuals to track and manage their health information.  
It maintains user profiles, including lists of current medications, medical history, and related health data.  
Key features include medication data entry forms, a medical knowledge base of drug interactions, and tools for users to check for potential conflicts among their medications to enhance safety and informed decision-making.

## Environment Rules / Constraints:  
- Only medications with active_status = true are considered for interaction checking.
- Drug interactions are checked only among active medications in a user's current list.
- Each medication referenced must exist in the Medication entity.
- Interactions must be cross-checked both ways (medication_id_1 ↔ medication_id_2).
public_context.task:
- For user USR001 (Alice Chan), replace Cetirizine due to the high-severity interaction with Ventolair:
  - Add a new medication record: medication_id=“MED-LORAT10”, name=“Loratadine”, dosage=“10 mg”, frequency=“once daily (morning)”, start_date=“2025-10-23”, end_date=“2026-10-22”.
  - Assign MED-LORAT10 to USR001 with active_status=True.
  - Set active_status=False for RX7759 (Cetirizine) in USR001’s user_medications.

- For user USR_S144 (Maya Singh), start a 7-day Amoxicillin course and update interactions:
  - Add a new medication record: medication_id=“MED-AMOX-25”, name=“Amoxicillin”, dosage=“500 mg”, frequency=“every 8 hours (three times daily)”, start_date=“2025-10-23”, end_date=“2025-10-30”.
  - Assign MED-AMOX-25 to USR_S144 with active_status=True.
  - Set active_status=False for MED-IRON7 (Ferrosanol) in USR_S144’s user_medications for the duration of the antibiotic course.
  - Add drug interaction entries to the knowledge base for the new Amoxicillin record, in both directions:
    - medication_id_1=“MED-AMOX-25”, medication_id_2=“MDX23-B”, interaction_type=“antagonistic”, interaction_description=“Amoxicillin may decrease the effectiveness of Glucozide MR in blood sugar regulation.”, severity=“moderate”.
    - medication_id_1=“MDX23-B”, medication_id_2=“MED-AMOX-25”, interaction_type=“antagonistic”, interaction_description=“Amoxicillin may decrease the effectiveness of Glucozide MR in blood sugar regulation.”, severity=“moderate”.
    - medication_id_1=“MED-AMOX-25”, medication_id_2=“MED-IRON7”, interaction_type=“chelation”, interaction_description=“Ferrosanol may lower oral absorption of amoxicillin if taken together.”, severity=“moderate”.
    - medication_id_1=“MED-IRON7”, medication_id_2=“MED-AMOX-25”, interaction_type=“chelation”, interaction_description=“Ferrosanol may lower oral absorption of amoxicillin if taken together.”, severity=“moderate”.

function.description:
Fetch a user's demographic and health profile information by user ID.

Args:
    user_id (str): The unique identifier of the user.

Returns:
    dict:
        On success:
            {
                "success": True,
                "data": UserInfo   # All profile info for the user
            }
        On failure:
            {
                "success": False,
                "error": str   # Reason for failure (e.g., user not found)
            }

Constraints:
    - User ID must exist in the system.
function.name: get_user_by_id

function.description:
Retrieve the list of all medications currently mapped to a user (regardless of active status).

Args:
    user_id (str): The unique user ID.

Returns:
    dict: 
        - If user exists: {
            "success": True,
            "data": List[dict], 
                # Each dict is {
                #   "medication_info": MedicationInfo,
                #   "active_status": bool
                # }
            }
        - If user does not exist: {
            "success": False,
            "error": "User does not exist"
        }

Constraints:
    - User must exist in users collection.
    - Only mapped medications are reported.
    - If a mapping references a non-existent medication, it is skipped.
function.name: list_user_medications

function.description:
Retrieve all medications a user is currently taking (where active_status=True).

Args:
    user_id (str): The unique id of the user.

Returns:
    dict: {
        "success": True,
        "data": List[MedicationInfo],  # List of active MedicationInfo for the user (may be empty)
    }
    or
    {
        "success": False,
        "error": str  # Description of the error, e.g. user/medication does not exist
    }

Constraints:
    - Only medications with active_status=True for that user are considered.
    - Each medication referenced must exist in the Medication entity.
function.name: list_active_user_medications

function.description:
Retrieve details for a specific medication by its medication_id.

Args:
    medication_id (str): The unique identifier for the medication.

Returns:
    dict: {
        "success": True,
        "data": MedicationInfo  # Medication details (name, dosage, etc.)
    }
    or
    {
        "success": False,
        "error": str  # Error message if medication not found
    }

Constraints:
    - The medication_id must exist in the Medication entity.
function.name: get_medication_by_id

function.description:
Confirm if a medication_id exists in the Medication entity.

Args:
    medication_id (str): Unique identifier for the medication.

Returns:
    dict:
        success: True if query processed, False for improper input.
        data: True if medication exists, False otherwise.
        error: Only present if improper input/parameters.

Constraints:
    - medication_id must be provided and be a string.
function.name: check_medication_existence

function.description:
Retrieve medication details for a supplied list of medication IDs.

Args:
    medication_ids (List[str]): List of medication IDs to query.

Returns:
    dict: {
        "success": True,
        "data": List[MedicationInfo],  # Info for each found medication_id, order preserved as in exists
    }
    or
    {
        "success": False,
        "error": str  # Error description (e.g. invalid input type)
    }

Constraints:
    - Each medication returned must exist in the Medication entity.
    - IDs not found are simply omitted from the result; no failure if partial exists.
function.name: get_medication_info_bulk

function.description:
For a given list of (active) medication IDs, retrieve all possible drug interactions from the knowledge base.
Cross-checks both directions: (A, B) and (B, A).

Args:
    medication_ids: List[str] — List of active medication IDs for a user.

Returns:
    dict:
      {
        "success": True,
        "data": List[DrugInteractionInfo],  # All found interactions among given medications
      }
    or
      {
        "success": False,
        "error": str  # Reason for failure (e.g. medication ID does not exist)
      }

Constraints:
    - All medication_ids must exist in the medications entity.
    - Both (A, B) and (B, A) must be checked against the interactions knowledge base.
function.name: get_drug_interactions_all_pairs

function.description:
Retrieve the interaction information between two medication IDs, 
checking both possible directions as per the knowledge base.

Args:
    medication_id_1 (str): First medication ID.
    medication_id_2 (str): Second medication ID.

Returns:
    dict: {
        "success": True,
        "data": DrugInteractionInfo
    }
    or
    {
        "success": False,
        "error": str
    }

Constraints:
    - Both medication_id_1 and medication_id_2 must exist in self.medications.
    - Interactions must be checked in both directions (medication_id_1 ↔ medication_id_2).
function.name: get_drug_interaction

function.description:
Assign a medication to a user, with the specified initial active/inactive status.

Args:
    user_id (str): Identifier of the user.
    medication_id (str): Identifier of the medication.
    active_status (bool): True if currently active, False otherwise.

Returns:
    dict: {
        "success": True,
        "message": "Medication assigned to user."
    }
    or
    dict: {
        "success": False,
        "error": "Reason for failure: user not found, medication not found, or already assigned."
    }

Constraints:
    - User must exist in the system.
    - Medication must exist in the system.
    - No duplicate assignment for a user-medication pair.
function.name: add_medication_to_user

function.description:
Set the active_status (activate/deactivate) of a user's medication mapping.

Args:
    user_id (str): User identifier.
    medication_id (str): Medication identifier.
    active_status (bool): Desired status (True = activate, False = deactivate).

Returns:
    dict: {
        "success": True,
        "message": "Medication status updated for user."
    }
    or
    {
        "success": False,
        "error": str  # Reason for failure.
    }

Constraints:
    - User must exist.
    - Medication must exist.
    - User-medication mapping must exist in the system.
function.name: update_user_medication_status

function.description:
Remove an assigned medication from a specific user's medication list.

Args:
    user_id (str): The user's unique identifier.
    medication_id (str): The medication's unique identifier to remove.

Returns:
    dict: 
        Success: { "success": True, "message": "Medication removed from user." }
        Failure: { "success": False, "error": "<reason>" }

Constraints:
    - User must exist.
    - Medication must exist.
    - The user-medication mapping must exist (otherwise removal fails).
    - All matching mappings are removed.
function.name: remove_medication_from_user

function.description:
Add a new medication record to the Medication entity.

Args:
    medication_id (str): Unique identifier for the medication.
    name (str): Name of the medication.
    dosage (str): Dosage instruction.
    frequency (str): How often the medication is taken.
    start_date (str): When medication usage starts.
    end_date (str): When medication usage ends.

Returns:
    dict: {
        "success": True,
        "message": "Medication added successfully."
    }
    or
    {
        "success": False,
        "error": "Reason for failure."
    }

Constraints:
    - medication_id must be unique (no existing entry).
    - All parameters are required, must be non-empty strings.
function.name: add_new_medication

function.description:
Add or update a drug interaction record in the knowledge base.

Args:
    medication_id_1 (str): ID of the first medication.
    medication_id_2 (str): ID of the second medication.
    interaction_type (str): Type/category of interaction.
    interaction_description (str): Description of the interaction.
    severity (str): Severity level of interaction.

Returns:
    dict: Success or failure result.

    - On success: { "success": True, "message": "Drug interaction added/updated." }
    - If either medication does not exist: { "success": False, "error": str }

Constraints:
    - Both medication_id_1 and medication_id_2 must exist in self.medications.
    - Interaction pairs are unordered (A,B or B,A), only one record per unordered pair.
    - Updates interaction if it already exists for the pair.
function.name: add_drug_interaction

function.description:
Deletes a drug interaction between two medications from the knowledge base.

Args:
    medication_id_1 (str): The ID of the first medication.
    medication_id_2 (str): The ID of the second medication.

Returns:
    dict: {
        "success": True,
        "message": "Drug interaction removed for <medication_id_1> and <medication_id_2>."
    }
    or
    {
        "success": False,
        "error": "Drug interaction not found for specified medications."
    }

Constraints:
    - Interactions must be cross-checked both ways (medication_id_1 ↔ medication_id_2).
    - All interactions matching this pair are removed.
function.name: remove_drug_interaction
